name: Year of Africa
short_desc: Seventeen African countries gain independence in a major wave of decolonization.
location: Africa · Cameroon · Togo · Madagascar · DR Congo · Somalia · Benin · Niger · Burkina Faso · Côte d’Ivoire · Chad · Central African Republic · Republic of the Congo · Gabon · Senegal · Mali · Nigeria · Mauritania
date_note: The seventeen-country convention counts independence milestones during 1960, including Senegal and Mali after the Mali Federation and Somalia’s unification. African decolonization began earlier and continued later.
notes: Added after a catalog gap review on 24 October 2026. Adds the continent-wide decolonization turning point instead of representing African independence through isolated conflicts alone. Evidence and date rationale: The seventeen-country convention refers to independence milestones during calendar year 1960, including Senegal and Mali after the Mali Federation and Somalia’s unification. It is not the beginning or completion of decolonization across Africa. Country labels are present-day geographic references. Primary evidence: https://www.un.org/dppa/decolonization/history/former-trust-and-nsgts. Cached Wikipedia introduction and lead image provide separately attributed background. Remains review, not comprehensive factual approval.
